claim: A Duke SE11 swinging-door effector moves only when an ST23 sector is operated and an SE11 in that ST23 sector shares its hitag; the operator sets T5 on every same-hitag SE11 and actors.cpp moves an SE11 only while T5 is set. An SE11 with no same-hitag ST23 operator is inert: its room never turns.
evidence: reference/eduke32/source/duke3d/src/sector.cpp:961-1000 (ST23 case: finds the SE11 in its own sector, then arms every SE11 with that hitag)
reference/eduke32/source/duke3d/src/actors.cpp:7292 (SE_11 moves only while pData[4] is set)
E4L1 sprite 487 (hitag 409, plain room 152) has no hitag-409 ST23; E1L2 room 262 is a second case
use: Convert an SE11 without a same-hitag ST23 as a static room, not a rotor; keep the room's other signals.

checked.how: sector.cpp:961-1000 read (G_OperateSectors, case ST_23_SWINGING_DOOR): finds an SE_11 in its own sector with !T5, then sets T5 = 1 on every SE_11 with sprite[j].hitag. actors.cpp:7292 case SE_11_SWINGING_DOOR, :7299 'if (pData[4])' gates the motion. Duke E4L1 (read_duke_map): sprite 487 SE11 hitag 409 in sector 152 (lotag 0); ST23 sectors 15,16,24,50,61,95,317,318,327,328,369,410 hold no SE11 of hitag 409. E1L2: sprite 250 hitag 284 in sector 262 is the only SE11 with no same-hitag SE11 in an ST23 sector.
